Air Quality 0 to 50: Switch to Active Mobility: Bike or walk for short trips (under 2 miles) instead of driving.
Conduct Regular Vehicle Maintenance: Keep engine filters clean and tires properly inflated to maintain optimal fuel efficiency and minimize exhaust.
Use Zero-VOC Paints & Cleaners: Opt for low/no-volatile organic compound products for household upkeep to avoid chemical emissions.
Transition Lawn Care to Electric: Replace gas-powered lawnmowers and leaf blowers with battery-electric alternatives.
Optimize Home Energy Efficiency: Seal drafty doors/windows and switch to LED lighting to lower power plant demand.
Practice Smart Fireplace Usage: Avoid burning wood or trash at home, choosing cleaner heating methods where possible.
Plant Native Trees & Shrubs: Grow native flora around your living space to act as natural carbon sinks and air filters.
Organize a Neighborhood Carpool Network: Build a community app or roster to share rides for school drop-offs and commutes.
Coordinate Community Tree Planting Events: Partner with local urban forestry programs to expand street canopies and green spaces.
Establish School/Workplace "No-Idle" Zones: Launch a community campaign to ban idling engines outside school pick-up spots and offices.
Air Quality 51 to 100: Combine Daily Errands: Group multiple errands into a single trip to minimize cold-engine driving cycles.
Use Public Transportation: Choose buses, light rail, or trains over personal vehicle driving during peak rush hours.
Avoid High-VOC Products on Sunny Days: Refrain from painting, solvent use, or applying lawn chemicals on warm, stagnant days when ozone forms easily.
Reschedule Lawn Mowing to Evening: Operate gas equipment in the cooler evening hours to reduce daylight ground-level ozone formation.
Conserve Indoor Energy: Lower air conditioning or heating usage by a few degrees during peak demand hours.
Consolidate Online Purchases: Minimize delivery vehicle trips by choosing combined shipping dates for packages.
Maintain Home HVAC Filters: Install MERV 11+ or HEPA filters in furnace/HVAC systems to catch rising ambient particulate matter.
Launch "Bike-to-Work / Car-Free Day" Campaigns: Organize city or office-wide events that incentivize non-motorized commuting.
Advocate for Clean Energy Tariffs: Group with local neighborhood associations to request community solar programs from local utilities.
Run Anti-Burn Public Awareness Drives: Organize local outreach reminding residents not to burn agricultural debris or yard waste on moderate-risk days.
Air Quality 101+: Set Vehicle HVAC to Recirculate Air: Prevent polluted outside air from entering your vehicle cabin while driving.
Seal Doors and Windows: Keep home doors and windows closed tight and seal gaps with weatherstripping.
Run HEPA Air Purifiers Indoors: Keep high-efficiency particulate air purifiers operating in primary living spaces.
Postpone Outdoor Exertion: Move workouts indoors or reschedule heavy physical labor to prevent inhaling deep particulates.
Wear N95/P100 Respirators: Wear a properly fitted N95 mask if you must go outdoors during high particulate matter ($	ext{PM}_{2.5}$) events.
Avoid Indoor Smoke Sources: Do not burn candles, incense, or use gas stoves without exhaust fans during poor air quality days.
Avoid Driving Unless Necessary: Delay non-essential driving entirely to avoid adding to regional emergency pollution levels.
Create Community Clean Air Shelters: Coordinate with local centers, libraries, or gyms to establish public indoor spaces equipped with heavy-duty air filtration.
Distribute N95 Masks to Vulnerable Populations: Partner with non-profits to supply masks and air filters to unhoused community members and low-income seniors.
Organize Emergency Remote Work / School Directives: Coalition with local business boards and school districts to trigger work-from-home days during extreme smog or wildfire smoke advisories.
